msg: Ingress object still routed by the retired ingress-nginx controller
fix: the ingress-nginx project stopped shipping releases and CVE fixes in March 2026 — move this rule set to a Gateway API HTTPRoute on a maintained controller
an unclassed Ingress is silently ignored by every controller that does not set itself as cluster default — set spec.ingressClassName, or move to HTTPRoute.parentRefs
replaced by spec.ingressClassName since Kubernetes 1.18; in Gateway API this is HTTPRoute.parentRefs[].name

msg: AKS HTTP application routing add-on class referenced
fix: that AKS add-on was retired — use the managed application routing ingressClassName, or a Gateway API GatewayClass
snippet annotations are refused by default since ingress-nginx v1.9 (allow-snippet-annotations=false) — rewrite as explicit HTTPRoute filters
refused by default since v1.9 and a named vector in the IngressNightmare advisory chain — express the intent as HTTPRoute filters
no Gateway API equivalent — model the TCP/UDP listener as a Gateway listener with a TCPRoute or UDPRoute
refused with the other snippet annotations — carry the auth call in an ExternalAuth extension of your Gateway implementation
Gateway API core: HTTPRoute filters[].type RequestMirror with requestMirror.backendRef
Gateway API core: HTTPRoute filters[].type URLRewrite with urlRewrite.path.replacePrefixMatch
Gateway API core: a separate HTTPRoute rule matching / with filters[].type RequestRedirect and requestRedirect.path
HTTPRoute core matches are Exact and PathPrefix only — RegularExpression path match is an experimental-channel feature, confirm your controller ships it
Gateway API core: HTTPRoute filters[].type RequestRedirect with requestRedirect.hostname and statusCode
Gateway API core: an HTTPRoute on the port-80 listener with filters[].requestRedirect.scheme https and statusCode 301
Gateway API core: add the name to HTTPRoute.spec.hostnames[]

Gateway API core: one HTTPRoute with two backendRefs carrying weight values, or a headers match for canary-by-header
Gateway API core: HTTPRoute rules[].timeouts.request and timeouts.backendRequest as Go durations
no Gateway API core equivalent — rate limiting lives in an implementation policy object, name it before you cut over
no Gateway API core equivalent — this becomes an implementation-specific BackendTrafficPolicy on the Service

msg: external auth subrequest declared by annotation
fix: no Gateway API core equivalent — every request past this route loses its auth check on cutover unless you port it to an ExternalAuth filter or a sidecar

msg: IP allow/deny list declared by annotation
fix: no Gateway API core equivalent — reproduce it as a NetworkPolicy or an implementation AuthorizationPolicy before cutover
Gateway API: the CORS filter is experimental-channel — until your controller ships it, use ResponseHeaderModifier
Gateway API: a Gateway listener with tls.mode Passthrough plus a TLSRoute — TLSRoute is experimental-channel
Gateway API core: set Service.spec.ports[].appProtocol (kubernetes.io/h2c for GRPC/h2c), or use a GRPCRoute

msg: request body size limit declared by annotation
fix: no Gateway API core equivalent — carry the limit into your controller's policy object or the application itself
